fields.topology_type: Multi-master single-channel shared serial bus; multidrop wired-AND with bitwise IDENTIFIER arbitration. The M_CAN controller is one node on this bus, attached via external transceiver. Internally, the M_CAN exposes a Host CPU register interface (Generic Slave) + external Message RAM interface (Generic Master) + optional DMU + TSU + Extension interfaces.

supported_topologies.name: Linear bus (typical automotive)
supported_topologies.description: All CAN nodes tap onto a single twisted-pair (ISO 11898-2 high-speed); terminated at both ends. CAN FD enables faster data phase on the same wire.

supported_topologies.name: Star / branched (low-speed)
supported_topologies.description: ISO 11898-3 fault-tolerant low-speed CAN allows branched topology (typical body electronics). CAN FD compatible if transceiver supports.

supported_topologies.name: Optical fibre
supported_topologies.description: Physical layer optional; CAN FD frame format is unchanged.

supported_topologies.name: Mixed Classical + CAN FD network
supported_topologies.description: Classical-CAN-only nodes coexist with CAN FD nodes ONLY if the FD nodes never transmit FD frames while Classical nodes are active. CAN FD nodes can transmit Classical frames (Tx Buffer FDF = 0) to coexist.

supported_topologies.name: Multiple M_CANs sharing one Message RAM
supported_topologies.description: M_CAN's Generic Master Interface supports M_CAN-to-M_CAN Message RAM sharing arbitration; one Message RAM (max 16K × 32-bit) can serve multiple CAN channels.

supported_topologies.name: Partial networking (ISO 11898-6 transceiver)
supported_topologies.description: Wake-up via dedicated wake-up frame at low power; transceiver handles partial wake-up, M_CAN unaware.

supported_topologies.name: Time-Triggered CAN (TTCAN, ISO 11898-4)
supported_topologies.description: Use CCCR.DAR = 1 to disable automatic retransmission; software runs the time-triggered schedule above M_CAN.

master_slave_role_summary.description: A unit originating a message; stays transmitter until bus idle or arbitration is lost.
A unit that is not transmitter and the bus is not idle.
Normal operation; sends ACTIVE ERROR FLAGs (6 dominant); CAN FD ESI = dominant.
Degraded operation; sends only PASSIVE ERROR FLAGs (6 recessive); adds SUSPEND TRANSMISSION after own messages; CAN FD ESI = recessive.
Not allowed to influence the bus; output drivers off; CCCR.INIT held = 1; requires CPU intervention to attempt recovery.
Receives data + remote frames + sends ACK; does NOT send error/data/remote/overload frames. Useful for bit-rate detection.
Receive only; cannot drive dominant bits; TXBRP held in reset.

fields.interconnect_role: There is no protocol-layer interconnect (no router / bridge) on the CAN bus. The bus is a flat shared medium; any node can transmit when the bus is idle, and bitwise arbitration on IDENTIFIER resolves contention without information loss. Inside the M_CAN, the Generic Master Interface arbitrates Tx Handler vs Rx Handler accesses to the external Message RAM (single- or dual-ported).

ordering_guarantees.single_bus: All nodes simultaneously see the same bus value (modulo signal propagation); data consistency = a message is accepted by all receivers or by none.
ordering_guarantees.arbitration: Higher-priority messages (lower IDENTIFIER value) are transmitted first; no fairness guarantee for equal-priority messages — re-arbitration each time.
ordering_guarantees.tx_fifo: Tx FIFO transmits in put-order (oldest message first).
ordering_guarantees.tx_queue: Tx Queue transmits by lowest Message ID (highest-priority message first); transmission order unpredictable when multiple queue buffers share Message ID.
ordering_guarantees.rx_fifo: Rx FIFO writes in arrival order; FIFO Get Index advanced explicitly by host via FIFO Acknowledge register.
ordering_guarantees.rx_buffer: Dedicated Rx Buffer locked by New Data flag until host writes 1 to clear; while locked, the filter element directing to this buffer will not match (acceptance filtering continues to next match).

memory_vs_peripheral_regions.M_CAN_register_space: 512 bytes; word-aligned 32-bit; accessible via Host CPU's 8/16/32-bit Generic Slave Interface.
memory_vs_peripheral_regions.Message_RAM_space: External (single- or dual-ported); up to 4.25K × 32-bit per M_CAN; partitioned into 11-bit Filter / 29-bit Filter / Rx FIFO 0 / Rx FIFO 1 / Rx Buffers / Tx Event FIFO / Tx Buffers (in any sequence; integrator-configurable via start addresses).

slave_classification.addressable_target: Not applicable on the CAN bus — CAN is content-addressed, not destination-addressed. All nodes see every frame; acceptance filtering happens locally on the IDENTIFIER.
slave_classification.data_producer: Any node may transmit DATA FRAMEs with one or more IDENTIFIERs.
slave_classification.data_consumer: Any node may apply acceptance filtering to accept matching IDENTIFIERs.
slave_classification.M_CAN_as_Host_slave: M_CAN's Generic Slave Interface presents 512-byte register space to the Host CPU. Indirectly addresses external Message RAM via dedicated registers + filter / buffer indices.
slave_classification.M_CAN_as_Master: Generic Master Interface initiates 32-bit read / write to external Message RAM.

wake_up_topology.wake_up_trigger: External clock controller deasserts m_can_clkstop_req (or CPU clears CCCR.CSR).
wake_up_topology.wake_up_message: CAN FD itself does not define a wake-up identifier (Classical CAN convention 'rrr rrrd rrrr'). Partial networking via ISO 11898-6 transceiver handles wake-up at the physical layer; M_CAN is bus-activity-agnostic at the protocol layer.
wake_up_topology.post_wake_sync: After clocks restart, M_CAN clears m_can_clkstop_ack + CCCR.CSA; CPU clears CCCR.INIT; BSP waits for 11 consecutive recessive bits (Bus_Idle) before joining bus.

two_clock_domains: Host clock domain (m_can_hclk) — Tx Handler, Rx Handler, Generic Slave, Generic Master, RAM Watchdog.
CAN clock domain (m_can_cclk) — CAN Core, Bit Stream Processor, Bit Timing Logic.
M_CAN_block_topology.sync_block: Cross-domain handoff between Host clock and CAN clock domains.
M_CAN_block_topology.interrupt_and_timestamp_block: Host-clock side; 16-bit CAN-bit-time counter for timestamps; routes IR to two CPU lines via ILS/ILE/IE.
M_CAN_block_topology.extension_interface_block: Host-clock side; routes all IR flags + selected status/control to external interrupt unit (optional).
